page: Amazon Web Services r5d.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 96 virtual CPUs (48 physical cores with 2 threads per core), 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression, multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only small block, read-only large block, and write large block operations all scoring in the top 25%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong performance in the top 25% tier.

The instance exhibits performance tradeoffs in compute-heavy tasks. LLM inference text generation is weak to poor, with 7B model text generation falling into the bottom 10%. However, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, combined with local NVMe SSD storage, makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, and high-throughput static web serving.

It delivers 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores, 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, backed by a 25 Gbps baseline network. While single-core benchmarks and LLM text generation speeds are weak, the instance excels in multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations, all ranking in the top 25% of benchmarks. This profile makes the instance suitable for large-scale databases, memory-intensive applications, and high-throughput web serving where local high-speed storage and large memory capacities are required.
